newsitem.title: USA: Drug stocks recover strongly on key upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Drug stocks recover strongly on key upgrade.

text.p: Major drug stocks surged Tuesday in a rebound from the previous day's plunge after Merrill Lynch upgraded industry leader Britol-Myers Squibb Co.

"What you're seeing in general in the group is a recovery from yesterday," said Merrill Lynch drug industry analyst Steve Tighe. His upgrade of Bristol-Myers to long-term buy from long-term accumulate was credited by some traders as sparking the drug sector stampede.

Bristol-Myers shares were up 8-1/4 to 84-5/8. Among other top drug stocks, Pfizer Inc. gained 4-5/8 to 115-5/8; Eli Lilly & Co. added 3-15/16 to 109-15/16; Merck & Co. Inc. was up 4-7/16 to 103-1/16; Warner-Lambert Co. rose 4-1/8 to 118-1/4 -- price swings of a sort seldom seen in the sector.
"The drug stocks are acting like the tech stocks today," said Gruntal & Co. drug industry analyst David Saks.

Institutional investors likely were pouring capital into Big Pharma, as the sector is known, on expectations of strong second-quarter earnings and amid general market bullishness on large-cap stocks, analysts said.
"Drug group fundamentals are exceptionally strong right now. It's the Dow stocks and the big index stocks that are doing well," said Alex. Brown drugs analyst Barbara Ryan.
"Coming into the end of the quarter, if people don't own them, they're going to look a little silly ... Some of this is a little bit of window-dressing for the end of the quarter," Ryan said.

The move marked a sharp reversal from Monday, when drug issues were among the hardest hit in a blue chip sell-off that saw the Dow Jones industrial average post its biggest percentage-point decline in almost a year.
"Some of this is a rebound off yesterday's decline," said drugs analyst Samuel Isaly, of Mehta & Isaly.
The Dow industrials ended up 153.80 points, or 2.02 percent, at 7,758.06 after Monday's 192-point drop, which was the second-steepest drop ever for the blue-chip index.
